records.title: Experimental studies on the conditioning of man for space flight
records.locator: Air University Quarterly Review 11(1), printed p. 68, Susceptibility to dysbarism
records.note: The investigator reports site-specific outcomes from Colorado and Morococha. The 38,000-ft test is described as standard exercise. The report identifies the number of people tested for these two outcome groups.

observations.locator: Air University Quarterly Review 11(1), printed p. 68, Susceptibility to dysbarism
observations.protocol: Prior residence described by Balke as 48 hours at 14,000 ft. Clark et al. describe two days at 14,160 ft (their reported 455 mm Hg). Standard exercise at 38,000 ft included repeated deep knee bends.
observations.outcome_window: During the one-hour chamber test in Clark et al. Both slight pains resolved by the end of the run.
observations.note: Balke reports 2 of 7. Clark et al. and NASA SP-117 describe the same outcome. NASA prints 446 mm Hg for the residence condition. The initial pressure remains source-specific.

observations.locator: Air University Quarterly Review 11(1), printed p. 68, Susceptibility to dysbarism
observations.protocol: Morococha chamber site at 14,800 ft. The dysbarism section describes the standard exercise test at 38,000 ft. Individual residence duration, acclimatization histories and gas delivery are unavailable.
observations.outcome_window: During the reported chamber test. Exact dwell and post-test observation were unspecified.
observations.note: The author identifies ten individuals who remained symptom-free. The denominator is people tested. The article does not provide attendance or per-person run histories.

records.title: Basic research problems in space medicine: a review
records.note: The investigators describe the same seven-person Mount Evans I program and two terminal tests on the same two Mount Evans II participants. The indexed original supplied the relevant pages during this review. Live PDF requests returned 404.

observations.locator: Clark et al. printed p. 576, two-hour bends test
observations.protocol: Two previously acclimatized subjects completed a ten-day sealed chamber exposure with varying effective altitude. On the final day a 40,000-ft decompression immediately followed the carbon dioxide experiment; oxygen masks were put on.
observations.outcome_window: Two hours at 40,000 ft. Post-test surveillance is unspecified.
observations.note: Clark et al. and Balke describe this same pair and symptom-free test. Their reports are linked to a single outcome group.

observations.locator: Clark et al. printed p. 576, pressure-suit exercise
observations.protocol: The same two participants donned pressure suits during the separate rapid decompression starting at 15,000 ft. They used helmets and oxygen during the procedure.
observations.outcome_window: Forty minutes at 50,000 ft. The reported finger pain disappeared toward the end of the exposure.
observations.note: Clark et al. explicitly describe one participant with finger pain. This detailed endpoint qualifies the preceding narrative phrase about a similar experience. The 40,000-ft observation uses the same two people.

additional_reported_history.outcome: Third-degree bends or chokes in all control experiments. An average of 18 minutes to severe symptoms. Exact number of control tests unknown.
No grade III symptoms. Mean time to grade II pain 50 minutes. Exact group and timed event counts unknown.
Forced descent after a mean of 53 minutes. Exact group and event counts unknown. NASA SP-117 describes this condition as similar to 10,000 ft.
No symptoms in supplemental tests with simulated piloting work following near-14,000-ft residence. Exact number of tests unknown.

records.title: Space-Cabin Atmospheres, Part III: Physiological Factors of Inert Gases
records.locator: NASA SP-117, printed p. 64 and references 15 and 99
records.note: Corroborates two slight-pain outcomes among seven Mount Evans subjects. Its 446 mm Hg differs from the 455 mm Hg in Clark et al. Its description of the 6,000-ft condition differs from Clark et al. Both values and wordings remain source-specific.
